subject: Chemistry
title: Box Jellyfish: Ocean's Deadliest Sting
description: One-minute skill: Box Jellyfish: Ocean's Deadliest Sting.

hook.text: The Australian box jellyfish can kill a human in under five minutes. Its venom attacks heart, nerves, and skin.

buildup.text: Each tentacle has millions of nematocysts—microscopic harpoons that inject venom on contact.

discovery.text: The venom creates pores in cell membranes, allowing potassium to flood out. Heart cells lose their electrical rhythm.

twist.text: Vinegar deactivates unfired nematocysts on skin. But once venom is injected, vinegar does nothing.

climax.text: An antivenom exists, but it must be given within minutes. Most victims die before reaching a hospital.

punchline.text: Pores in cell membranes, potassium floods out. The heart loses its beat.

quiz.question: How does box jellyfish venom kill so quickly?
options: It creates pores in cells that disrupt the heart's electrical rhythm
It blocks oxygen from entering the lungs
It causes the brain to swell rapidly

details.summary: The box jellyfish Chironex fleckeri delivers venom through billions of microscopic nematocysts on its tentacles that inject cardiotoxins and neurotoxins simultaneously. The venom can cause cardiac arrest within minutes, making it the most venomous marine creature known.
details.whyItMatters: Box jellyfish stings kill dozens of people annually in tropical waters. Research into their venom has led to better emergency treatments and understanding of pore-forming toxins.
takeaways: Nematocysts fire at incredible acceleration to inject venom
The venom attacks the heart, nervous system, and skin simultaneously
Vinegar application prevents unfired nematocysts from discharging

faq.question: Why is vinegar the recommended first aid for box jellyfish stings?
faq.answer: Vinegar's acetic acid prevents undischarged nematocysts still on the skin from firing additional venom. It does not neutralize venom already injected but stops further envenomation. Fresh water triggers nematocyst discharge and should never be used on stings.

faq.question: How quickly can a box jellyfish sting kill an adult human?
faq.answer: Severe stings from Chironex fleckeri can cause cardiac arrest within two to five minutes. The venom creates pores in cell membranes, causing massive potassium leakage that disrupts the heart's electrical rhythm. Immediate CPR and antivenom are essential for survival.
